newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia posts gains in 1H intl air travel.
newsitem.headline: Colombia posts gains in 1H intl air travel.

text.p: The number of international air passengers traveling to and from Colombia rose 8.46 percent to 1.24 million in the first half of this year against the same period last year, the Civil Aviation Authority said Thursday.
The number of international passenger arrivals was up 9.98 percent to 592,158 while the number of departures was up 7.11 percent to 652,409.
U.S carrier Continental Airlines posted the biggest gain, transporting 58,714 passengers to and from Colombia in the first half of this year -- a 94.1 percent increase.

with 32,914 international passengers to and from the country while Colombia's main carrier Avianca, part of the Santo Domingo industrial group, transported 447,660 passengers on international flights between January to June -- a 19.1 percent increase.
Air France flew 19,789 international Colombia-bound passengers, 18.4 percent up on the first half of 1996 while Italy's Alitalia posted a 17.9 percent gain with 11,285 passengers.

British Airways reported a 10.7 percent gain with 18,781 passengers in and out of Colombia while Lufthansa's international passenger volume in the January to June period was up 9.91 percent to 21,198 people.
American Airlines flew 188,783 passengers to and from Colombia in the year to June, a 2.24 percent increase.
Over the same period, passengers on domestic services dropped 8.09 percent to 3.7 million.
Avianca's domestic passenger volume fell 14.04 percent to 1.32 million.

Aerolineas Centrales de Colombia's domestic passenger volume fell by more than 4 percent to 805,678. The only domestic airline to post gains was state-run airline Satena, up more than 27 percent with 141,206 passengers.
